title: Stellantis and the future of the Canadian auto industry
summary: What the Stellantis saga can tell us about the Canada-US relationship and the future of the Canadian auto industry.

blocks.text: What the Stellantis saga can tell us about the Canada-US relationship and the future of the Canadian auto industry.
Front Burner26:15Stellantis and the future of the Canadian auto industry

Last week, Prime Minister Mark Carney had scathing words for Stellantis, the multinational auto manufacturer that makes cars like Jeeps and Chryslers. He was reacting to the news that the company was selling its idled plant in Brampton, Ontario to a Canadian armoured vehicle maker called Roshel, calling it a “betrayal of workers.” The federal government has since both threatened to sue the company and described an "aggressive package" to prevent the sale.

The whole saga goes back years and can serve as a window into a whole bunch of issues facing our country right now. From trade turmoil and our interdependence on the U.S., to corporate welfare and the protection of taxpayer dollars, to the future of the Canadian auto industry. Jayme Poisson speaks with Joanna Smith, a reporter with the Canadian business and tech outlet the Logic where she covers trade.
